drafts.walkScript: Her words about the wardrobe start at line 10. Line 11 says 'In a cupboard meant for clothes'. Line 12 asks what she sees 'at the bottom but a heap of rolls'. So at the bottom of the wardrobe is a heap of rolls. The 'horror' on line 9 is on her own face, not in the wardrobe.

Line 35 says they had the sandwiches 'on the crate at one o'clock'. Line 36 says he got 'through half of his'. The same line says he 'passed' the rest over. So he ate half and gave away the other half. The enormous breakfast on line 36 is only what he said, not what he did.

Line 5 says 'From here she can see the', and the sentence runs on. Line 6 finishes it: 'place under the roof where two boards have pulled apart'. So what she sees is a gap where two boards have parted. The flagstone on line 5 is where she stands, not what she sees. Line 7 says 'Her eyes do the counting', so she can count them.

Line 26 is what Grandad says about the mower. He says 'Mower out, and your mum comes home to a garden she recognises'. A garden she 'recognises' is a garden she knows. So the mower is for her mum coming home to a garden she knows. The hand on the door on line 25 is not a reason for the mower.
